output.digest:
Creative Analytics Digest (last 3 months). We reviewed 32 ads. What won: The top performers featured the copy “nirvana_ivy_pro​_hear_music_the_way_it_was_meant_to_be_heard_with_nirvana_ivy_pr,” which outperformed the account average by 66%. Ads with female talent, calm mood, indoor home environment, and copy focused on meetings also beat averages by over 60%. Green and trendy color schemes delivered 34% and 33% lifts respectively, with black and purple colors also showing strong gains.

What lost: Ads using urgency as a hook underperformed by 16%, with benefit-led offers falling short by 26%. Moderate pacing and red color usage were notably weak, delivering roughly half the account average performance. Upbeat music and music-only audio also dragged results down by nearly 49%, indicating these elements didn’t resonate well.

The bigger picture: The strongest cross-crystal pattern among top ads combined a studio mode with no offer, delivering a 64% performance boost. This suggests next briefs should focus on clean, studio-shot creatives without overt promotional offers, emphasizing calm, indoor settings and trending color palettes to maximize engagement.

Ads to scale: 52523712116417, 52569418992617, 52650815761017 — strong performance indexes with below-average spend share; consider scaling budget.  
Ads to pause: 52523712116217, 52523700926417, 52523703850217 — underperform on ROAS and CPA relative to account averages; consider pausing or reducing spend.
